audience.notes: Australian couples in their 30s, luxury, AUD 150K+, planning from Australia for an overseas wedding. Couple's top 2 fears: (1) the wrong planner or a team that drops the ball; (2) planning from the other side of the world with no one on the ground. The paying parent cares about older guests coping (heat, stairs, boats) and nothing going missing. Do not write for the bargain hunter: no budget hacks, no dupes, no 'pack light to save on fees'.

payload.search_intent: Informational with a printable, save-it intent: a sectioned list they can tick off, plus trustworthy rules for leaving and re-entering Australia.
payload.angle: The printable destination wedding packing list for Australians, split by who packs what: the couple, the guests, the wedding-day kit, and the documents and carry-on bag that never leaves you. Australian travel rules are linked at the claim from official sources, and a closing section shows what a Wedded Advisor arranges on the ground so it never has to go in a suitcase.
serp_gaps_to_win: Positions 1 to 3 in all markets are pins, an Etsy listing, a Facebook post and a 2020 brand blog: a real editorial list can win.
Split by role (couple, guests, wedding-day kit, documents and carry-on): no ranking result does this.
Australian rules at the claim (Smartraveller, Border Force, biosecurity, TGA, CASA): no ranking result covers them.
What you do not need to pack because your advisor arranges it: nobody covers the invisible work.
Printable format: matches the Etsy and PDF intent in every image pack.

outline.h2: How to use this destination wedding packing list
outline.answers: What is on the list and how should we use it?
must_include: Primary keyword in the first 100 words
40 to 60 word quick answer: four lists (documents and carry-on, couple, wedding-day kit, guests) plus the rules for medicines, batteries and bringing things home

outline.h2: Documents and carry-on: the bag that never leaves you
outline.answers: What must be in hand luggage, not checked bags?
must_include: Checklist: passports (validity checked against the destination's rules), travel insurance details, copies of key documents stored separately and digitally, marriage paperwork, vendor contacts and run sheet, rings, the wedding outfit
Smartraveller on passports, insurance and pre-departure checklist, linked at the claim
Link /expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate for what paperwork travels with you
Link /destination-weddings/how-to-travel-with-wedding-dress for the dress (do not repeat its detail)
Link /all-the-practical-ways-to-keep-your-engagement-ring-safe-while-traveling for rings
Do NOT quote any airline's baggage or garment-bag rule; tell readers to check with their airline

outline.answers: What do we pack for every event across the wedding week?
must_include: Checklist by event (welcome drinks, ceremony and reception, farewell brunch, days off), plus climate layers and footwear for sand, grass, cobblestones
Wedding attire and accessories, beauty and grooming, chargers and adaptors
Groom or second partner's list, not bride-only
Short printable layout (tick boxes or compact lists), not prose

outline.answers: What should be in the day-of bag? (PAA: what should a bride pack for her wedding day?)
must_include: Emergency kit list: sewing kit, fashion tape, stain remover, blotting papers, pain relief, plasters, snacks, phone charger, vow cards, envelopes for any tips agreed in advance
Who carries it on the day (maid of honour, best man, planner)
Weather item: a plan, not just an umbrella (ties to the closing section)

outline.answers: What should our guests pack, and how do we tell them?
must_include: Guest list by event and dress code; comfortable shoes for the venue; sun and heat items; anything older guests need (medication, a light layer, flat shoes for uneven ground) for the paying parent
PAA: what not to wear: link /expert-advice/what-not-to-wear-to-a-wedding
Share the list on the wedding website or guest guide: link /destination-weddings/destination-wedding-guest-guide
Etiquette for travelling guests: link /destination-wedding-etiquette-10-questions-answered
Guest travel and accommodation: link /travel

outline.h2: Medicines, batteries and what you cannot bring home
outline.answers: What rules apply leaving and re-entering Australia?
must_include: Medicines: carry in original packaging with a prescription or doctor's letter, and check the destination's rules (Smartraveller travelling with medicine page and TGA travelling overseas with medicines page, linked at the claim)
Batteries: power banks and spare lithium batteries go in carry-on (CASA dangerous goods guidance, linked at the claim; the researcher confirms exact wording)

Coming home: declare flowers, seeds, food, wooden and natural items such as a dried bouquet or welcome-bag treats (Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry biosecurity page, linked at the claim)
Duty-free allowances and cash over the reporting threshold (Australian Border Force, linked at the claim; the researcher sources current figures, do not invent them)
Every rule attributed to its official source and dated; no airline-specific rules

outline.h2: What your Wedded Advisor arranges so you do not pack it
outline.answers: What should we not be carrying at all?
must_include: The invisible work: steaming and pressing on arrival, welcome bags sourced at the destination instead of packed from home, decor and stationery hired or shipped by vendors, wet-weather plan and umbrellas held at the venue, transfers sized for luggage and garment bags, room-block deliveries to guests' rooms
Answers couple fear 2 (planning from the other side of the world): someone on the ground receives and checks what arrives
Answers couple fear 1 (the wrong team): what a good planning team confirms in writing before you fly
Link /wonderland-concierge (service) and /plan-your-destination-wedding
Use only live brand wording from brand-profile.md; no Wedded World plug
